title: Pinflow-driven benchmark orchestration and profile artifact strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Improve the benchmark harness to produce deterministic, publishable performance profiles tied to pinned model versions and a discoverable profile registry. This ticket covers dataset sampling rules, prompt templating, eval-runner plugin enhancements, artifact naming/versioning, CI gating, and the publish/canary workflow to Console/Registry.

Scope:
- Add a "pinflow" mode to the harness which records the exact model binary+config (model_uri, commit, quantization profile) used for a run and embeds that into the profile artifact metadata.
- Define stable dataset sampling: support fixed-seed deterministic slices and a repeatable stratified-sampler for long tails. Allow generating both "canonical" (stable) and "stochastic" (variance) profile variants.
- Extend prompt templating to materialize prompt families with metadata describing temperature, stopping criteria, token budget, and canonicalization rules used for metrics.
- Eval runner plugin API: ensure runners can declare resource preferences (batching, kv-cache-required), fallback compatibility, and expose per-case outputs for quality metrics.
- Artifact scheme: profiles saved as profile-{model_semver}-{dataset_hash}-{date}.json with an accompanying manifest.yml that lists pinned model_uri, git_commit, quantization_tag, runner_version, and sampling_seed.
- Publish flow: CI job builds profile artifact, runs smoke-checks (latency/throughput P50/P95 bounds and minimal quality thresholds), and then uploads to private profile registry. Canary publish to Console (rollout to 5% of traffic) via a release job for Dedicated customers.

Non-goals: full UI work in Console (that will be separate ticket) and reworking the entire eval harness library surface (we only add extensions).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can run --pinflow and output artifact + manifest with model_uri+commit+quant_tag.
2) Deterministic canonical slice option implemented with seed documented in manifest.
3) Runner plugins can opt into resource hints and produce per-case QA outputs.
4) CI smoke checks exist and fail builds if P95 latency or quality fall below thresholds.
5) Profile artifacts successfully uploaded to profile-registry endpoint and visible in the registry index.
notes:
Design trade-offs and decisions: deterministic canonical profiles are prioritized for regression detection (trade-off: may not surface tail performance). We'll keep stochastic variant generation as optional to capture variance for SLO planning. Artifact naming uses dataset_hash rather than dataset name to avoid leaks of PII/partner names. We decided not to bake model weights into artifacts; instead we pin to an immutable model_uri and git_commit for reproducibility. Runner versioning will follow semver independent from harness.

Implementation plan:
- Week 1: add manifest metadata, model_uri capture, and deterministic sampler implementation.
- Week 2: prompt templating and plugin surface for runner hints.
- Week 3: CI smoke checks + upload integration to profile-registry.
- Week 4: canary publish job and docs.

Open questions:
- Should the manifest include a compile-time kernel fingerprint? (ops: useful for debugging perf deltas but increases surface). Proposal: record kernel selector name and hardware class, not full binary hash.
- Retention: how long should profile artifacts be kept in registry by default? Proposal: 90 days for auto-prune, with longer retention configurable per project.
